polityNote: Republic of Guinea throughout the scope. NE atoms are the 33 prefectures + Conakry (layout since 1985); the first-level units since 1994 are the seven administrative regions + Conakry, built here as unions of prefectures. NE quirk: four prefecture atoms (Boké, Faranah, Kankan, Kindia) carry the Wikidata QID of the region, not the prefecture.

unresolved.what: Guinea before 1994: four divisions (Guinée maritime, Moyenne, Haute, Forestière) over 33 prefectures + Conakry; earlier 29-33 «régions administratives»
unresolved.why: Two questions stay open. (1) Which units were first-level between 1985 and 1994: Binns says Guinea had four administrative divisions until 1994, but Statoids, FIPS 10-4 and the first ISO 3166-2 edition all treat the 33 prefectures + Conakry (called régions administratives before 1985) as the primary subdivisions, and no text was found that gives the four divisions a territory, a head or a date. The natural regions do not follow prefecture lines everywhere (e.g. Kissidougou). (2) The date of the 1994 regions is known only to the year. Before 1985 the 29 régions administratives differ from the prefectures by the 1985 splits (Coyah from Dubréka; Koubia and Lélouma from Labé; Lola from Nzérékoré; Mandiana from parts of Kankan and Siguiri), and the 1958-1980 changes are not listed by any source found.
